title: Request entropy sandbox and priority hooks
content:
Summary:
This note compiles recent customer asks that show high signal entropy — meaning the ask surface is noisy, inconsistent across accounts, and uncertain in implementation scope. The goal is not to finalize solutions but to create a small sandbox of experiments (priority hooks) that let eng/product validate impact quickly. Document purpose: create 4–6 pragmatic probes, assign owners, capture success criteria and quick-win patches.

How we measured entropy (practical heuristic):
- Pull 6 weeks of CS tickets, sales notes, and post-onboarding interviews (sample size ~42 accounts).
- For each ask, rate along three axes (0–3): prevalence, clarity, and implementation consensus.
- Entropy score = (3 - clarity) + (3 - implementation_consensus) + prevalence_weighted (0–3). Higher == noisier.
- Tagging done manually by two analysts (Marco, Linh) and spot-checked by SE.

Quick read: 6 fast probes recommended. Two immediate tactical fixes (<=5 dev days), two medium experiments (2–4 sprints), two research/metric plays (observability + eval).

Representative high-entropy asks (short vignettes):
1) "Per-request routing preferences" (entropy=7)
   - Customer asks: Route a subset of requests to cheaper quantized model variants while keeping another subset on high-quality model. Descriptions vary by customer: some want per-API-key, some want per-call flags, some want routing by intent detection.
   - Friction: No standard call-level metadata in current API; teams propose different semantics (pin model vs. score-based routing).
   - Example quote: "We need low-cost inference for bulk summarization but gold model for legal queries. Ideally in one call stack."

2) "Token-level billing reconciliation" (entropy=8)
   - Customer asks: Better breakdown of token-level cost for partial responses, streaming, and reranks. Some customers want post-call CSV export, others want in-console drilldowns.
   - Friction: Current billing aligns to aggregated token counts; edge cases (cancellations, retries) cause confusion and disputes.

3) "Embedding drift alerts" (entropy=6)
   - Ask: Detect when embeddings produced by a model drift relative to an indexed corpus (embedding mismatch causing retrieval failures). Some want threshold alerts; others want automatic reindexing.

4) "KV cache visibility and forced-evict" (entropy=7)
   - Ask: Fine-grained visibility into per-session KV cache usage and forced-eviction APIs to avoid stale context when reusing sessions across multi-tenant apps.

5) "Latency tail guarantees for small bursts" (entropy=5)
   - Ask: Customers report occasional high 95/99 latency during brief bursts. Requests for SLA-friendly small-burst lanes or priority ingress routing.

6) "Function calling semantics for partial failures" (entropy=6)
   - Ask: When a tool call fails mid-stream, what should the SDK surface? Options: explicit error + fallback to model, partial structured payload, or automatic retry. Fragmented preferences across customers.

Low-entropy, high-impact asks (quick wins):
- Per-route cost quickstats in Console (small UI + existing metrics): customers repeatedly ask for this and we have the backend events. Est dev: 3 days. Owner: Linh. Success metric: 20% reduction in billing support tickets for accounts in pilot.
- Streamed-response cancel semantics doc + example (doc + SDK snippet): clarify what happens on client cancellation for token billing and retry logic. Est effort: 2 days. Owner: Asha. Success metric: fewer follow-ups in support threads.

Priority hooks (probes) — proposed sandbox experiments: 
1) Routing Flags POC (owner: Ethan)
   - Scope: Add a per-call header X-rdwr-route: {cheap|balanced|gold}. Implement in gateway to route to three model-variants. No policy engine.
   - Hypothesis: 60% of routing asks are satisfied by simple per-call routing, lowering token spend by 25% for pilot customers.
   - Success criteria: pilot with 3 customers, observe correct routing and <=2% error rate. Measure cost delta and product satisfaction.
   - Est dev: 2 weeks (gateway + simple metric + docs). Dependencies: infra capacity for model variants, billing tagging (minor).

2) Token Billing CSV Export (owner: Linh)
   - Scope: Add downloadable CSV for last-30-day token events including call_id, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, charge_bucket.
   - Hypothesis: Offers transparency and reduces disputes.
   - Success: Pilot 10 accounts; ticket churn drop >=30% in billing queue after 6 weeks.
   - Est dev: 1.5 weeks (service + export + minimal UI).

3) Embedding Drift Canary (owner: Marco + Solutions Eng)
   - Scope: Build a lightweight canary that samples a chosen query set daily, computes embedding similarity distribution vs baseline, and alerts when mean similarity drops X sigma.
   - Hypothesis: Early detection prevents retrieval accuracy drop and reduces customer escalations.
   - Success: Trigger meaningful alerts for real customers during 4-week pilot and enable reindex workflow.
   - Est dev: 3–4 weeks (pipeline + alerting + small UI).

4) KV Cache Eviction API (research->prototype) (owner: SRE liaison)
   - Scope: Define API to list/evict session caches, plus Console control. Prototype for dedicated pools only.
   - Hypothesis: Reduces customer confusion when sessions share stale context; eases multi-tenant reuse patterns.
   - Success: One customer uses evict API to resolve a stale-context bug; positive feedback.
   - Est dev: 2 sprints (design + prototype).

5) Latency-burst lane experiment (owner: Platform Eng)
   - Scope: Configure a small priority queue (reserved burst tokens per-customer) routed to a tuned worker pool.
   - Hypothesis: A small reserved lane reduces observed 95/99 latencies during short bursts for pilot accounts.
   - Success: 95th latency percentile improvement of >=20% for pilot.
   - Est dev: 3–6 weeks (capacity + routing + telemetry).

6) Function-call failure contract (owner: SDK lead)
   - Scope: Propose an SDK contract: (a) explicit error callback, (b) optional partial payload delivery, (c) stable retry semantics. Append examples to SDK docs.
   - Hypothesis: A documented contract reduces integration variance and support back-and-forth.
   - Est dev: 1 sprint (spec + SDK + examples).

Prioritization rubric (for this sandbox):
- Score each probe on: customer-impact (0–5), cost-savings potential (0–5), dev effort (0–5, inverted), org dependencies (0–3).
- Probes with (impact+cost - effort) > 4 and org dependencies <=1 become top candidates for Q2 micro-sprints.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Routing flags without policy engine may create inconsistent expectations. Mitigation: Clear docs and limited pilot with annotated examples.
- Risk: Billing CSV exposes raw events that may confuse. Mitigation: Ship with an explainer and sample rows.
- Risk: Embedding drift false positives. Mitigation: conservative thresholds and manual verification step before alerts.

Open questions to resolve before pilot kickoff:
- Are dedicated pools required for KV-evict POC, or can we prototype on hosted lanes? (action: Platform Eng to confirm infra constraints)
- Billing: confirm that we can include call_id-level tagging without billing pipeline changes. (action: Finance + Billing Eng)
- Which 3 customers are best early-adopters for routing flags? Criteria: mid-to-high usage, mixed model needs, receptive SE contact. (action: CS to nominate by 2029-03-01)

Next steps (short list):
- This week: circulate to Platform Eng, Billing, and SDK leads for feasibility.
- Week +1: pick top 2 probes (Routing Flags & Token CSV) and assign tickets (Jira seeds: CS-4821 -> routing-probe, CS-4822 -> billing-csv).
- Week +2–4: implement quick wins and stand up pilot instrumentation.

Appendix / snips of raw customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We run large summarization jobs and will take 80% cheaper answers if we can keep a gold path for our legal flows." — Enterprise finance app
- "Billing export would let us reconcile dev/test churn and avoid repeated asks — we just want a CSV we can share with finance." — Marketplace customer
- "Sometimes our embeddings stop matching user queries; reindexing helped but we didn't know why it happened." — search product

References + quick links:
- Confluence playbook (internal): confluence:CS-entropy-playbook-982
- Seed Jira: jira:CS-4821, jira:CS-4822
- Slack thread: #cs-inference-threads (pinned messages)

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight. The goal is to fail small and learn. Use pilots to calibrate thresholds and expand only when we see clear ROI or loud customer concordance.

-- end --
